english: The sum $\displaystyle\sum_{k=3}^{14}\dfrac{\binom{k}{2}}{\binom{k}{3}\binom{k+1}{3}}$ can be written as $1-\dfrac{1}{N}$ for a positive integer $N$. Then the value of $N$ is ______.
hindi: योग $\displaystyle\sum_{k=3}^{14}\dfrac{\binom{k}{2}}{\binom{k}{3}\binom{k+1}{3}}$ को किसी धनात्मक पूर्णांक $N$ के लिए $1-\dfrac{1}{N}$ के रूप में लिखा जा सकता है। तब $N$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: Hence each term is $\dfrac{\binom{k+1}{3}-\binom{k}{3}}{\binom{k}{3}\binom{k+1}{3}}=\dfrac{1}{\binom{k}{3}}-\dfrac{1}{\binom{k+1}{3}}$ (valid for $k\ge3$, where $\binom{k}{3}\neq0$).
Summing from $k=3$ to $14$, the inner terms cancel: $\dfrac{1}{\binom{3}{3}}-\dfrac{1}{\binom{15}{3}}=1-\dfrac{1}{455}$.
originality_note: New: the numerator C(k,2) is exactly the Pascal difference of the two denominator factors, so the term splits as a difference of reciprocals of binomial coefficients (way 4, hidden telescoping). Closest known: telescoping sums 1/(k(k+1)) or hockey-stick sums of C(k,r). Different because: the telescoping happens in reciprocals of C(k,3) via Pascal's rule.

concept_use.Telescoping series involving binomial co: Pascal's rule turns the term into 1/C(k,3) - 1/C(k+1,3), which telescopes to 1 - 1/C(15,3).

stem_review: Read as a student: summation range stated, N positive integer and unique; answer 455 is a positive 3-digit integer as planned; Hindi mirrors. No change.
key_step: Recognise C(k,2) = C(k+1,3) - C(k,3) in the numerator.
justification: One standard identity followed by telescoping; routine but needs the right identity. Comparable to routine L2 anchors such as 2021-P1-Q18 (L2).
